Description: How far the low-degree pass in ``simplify_network`` goes; it runs to a fixed point, once, before the target-count aggregation. ``degree1and2`` iteratively eliminates every bus with one or two incident Lines: stubs fold into their single neighbour, and a degree-2 bus has its two segments combined in series, so the corridor is rated at its narrowest section and its demand weight and one-port assets are split between the two neighbours by the Kron factor. ``lossless`` folds stubs and splices out only the degree-2 buses that cost nothing: both Lines lead to distinct neighbours with equal ``s_nom``/``s_nom_min``/``s_nom_max``/``s_max_pu``/``s_nom_extendable``, and the bus holds no Generator, StorageUnit, Store or Link endpoint -- demand weight and Loads are allowed and split by the Kron factor, which is exact for fixed injections. It removes a strict subset of what ``degree1and2`` removes. ``false`` skips the pass. Parallel Lines are never merged in any mode, so an SSSC can be sited on either leg of a pair. ``true`` is still accepted as a synonym for ``degree1and2``; the retired ``degree1`` (stubs only) raises.

How a degree-2 series merge rates the corridor it builds. ``cost_weighted`` (default) takes ``sum_i c_i s_i / sum_i c_i`` over the segments, weighted by ``capital_cost``: with ``capital_cost`` summed, this is the rating at which a single slope is the asymptote of the true piecewise-linear expansion cost ``sum_i c_i (S - s_i)^+``, so it never overcharges and is exact once every segment binds. ``min`` takes the narrowest segment, which is the exact thermal limit but overcharges every expansion. ``s_nom_min``/``s_nom_max`` take the minimum either way.
Bus aggregation in ``simplify_network``: the caller names the cluster count and the distance references are calibrated from the network.

Whether to run the target-count aggregation at all. With this off and ``low_degree_reduction`` false the stage still converts voltage levels, removes transformers and aggregates to substations -- that last step is not optional.

Number of clusters this pass produces, and -- since it is the last reduction the stage applies -- the bus count of the exported network. Must be at least the number of connected subgraphs left once region boundaries are cut.

Dimensionless weight on the electrical term. 1.0 weights effective reactance and geographic distance equally at the scale of a typical line; above 1 favours electrical proximity, below 1 favours geographic proximity.
Random probes used to approximate effective reactance and to calibrate the reference scales.

Probe columns kept as clustering features, setting how faithfully the effective-reactance term is reproduced: the relative error of the estimate is sqrt(2 / n_feature_dims). A subsample of the probes rather than a projection of them, so that error stays uniform across scales instead of concentrating on the short distances that decide the early merges.
Seed for the probe draw and subsample. Fixing it makes the busmap reproducible.

How the Line pooled from the circuits two clusters share is rated. ``sum`` (default) adds the circuit ratings: the circuits end on different buses inside the clusters, so the unreduced network steers their split and can load all of them. ``parallel_bottleneck`` (pypsa's default) caps the bundle at the first circuit to saturate under a susceptance split. A number ``z`` rates it at ``bottleneck + z * (sum - bottleneck)``. Applies to ``s_nom``, ``s_nom_min`` and ``s_nom_max``; the substation aggregation always uses ``parallel_bottleneck``.
When building multiple networks, Use 'population' if you want to ensure the clusters are assigned constant names.
Implementation curerntly overrides to true. Network is simplified to substation nodes with positive or negative power injection.
Specifiy the method of aggregating fields within the generators, buses tables.
Specify the proportion of nodes to be attributed to a given zone in the form (California: 0.5) for half of all nodes to be located in California. Only used with TAMU Network
